transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (OptiRetail Head of Platform), Marcus Li (OptiRetail ML Engineer), Tara Nguyen (OptiRetail Security), Evan Park (OptiRetail SRE)

[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna do a technical deep dive on dedicated vs hosted, focus on perf, kv cache, batching and quant. feel free to interrupt, diego and aisha will handle the heavy lift on the runtime points.
[00:16] Priya: thanks, we've been hitting p95 spikes in production on our recommender, and noisy neighbor effects are our top worry. also need to know what guarantees you can offer for throughput.
[00:28] Diego: totally, that's exactly what we planned. quick high level: hosted gives you fastest onboarding and is multi-tenant with soft isolation, dedicated is isolated GPU pools with reserved throughput and stronger SLOs. but there's a lot in between — kv cache, batching, and quant profiles change the picture.
[00:45] Marcus: can you explain the noisy neighbor failure mode in hosted? like how often do we see it and is it predictable?
[00:56] Diego: short answer: in hosted you can get contention on shared infer nodes during bursty traffic which raises tail latencies. long answer: we have autoscaling and smart routing which mitigates it but it's not the same as dedicated capacity where you own N GPUs. sometimes the scheduler shifts requests across nodes and you see cache thrash.
[01:12] Tara: cache thrash — do you mean KV cache getting evicted? how deterministic is the prefix caching?
[01:20] Aisha: exactly. KV cache is per-worker and we do prefix caching when requests repeat similar prefixes. on hosted we rely on cross-tenant caching heuristics but eviction happens when memory pressure increases. on dedicated, if you pin capacity and enable sticky routing, you can keep a warm KV cache for a set of routes. less eviction, much better p95.
[01:40] Evan: sticky routing — that implies sticky sessions, right? does that reduce overall throughput?
[01:47] Diego: there is a tradeoff. sticky routing improves latency for repeated keys because cache hits go to same worker, but it may reduce global statistical batching efficiency — you lose some batching opportunities across routes. we recommend hybrid: for high-QPS routes you can enable sticky to keep latency tight, and allow others to flow into pooled batching.
[02:05] Priya: what's the ballpark p95 improvement we should expect if we move from hosted to dedicated for our recommender workload?
[02:13] Diego: depends a lot on model and seq length. for a 2k-context model with high repeat prompts and warm KV cache, we've seen p95 drop from ~420ms to ~210ms on Dedicated with sticky routing and warmed cache. but if your workload is single-shot, batching optimizations on hosted can be almost as good.
[02:37] Marcus: interesting, our workloads are 80% re-ranking with similar prefixes. we also use quantized weights to save cost — any gotchas?
[02:46] Aisha: quantization is great for cost/throughput but watch accuracy. 8-bit quant gives big perf wins on modern kernels, but some models need fine-tuning or PTQ calibration. runtime-wise, quantized kernels often have lower memory footprint so KV cache can hold more entries, which indirectly reduces tail latencies.
[03:06] Tara: from security/compliance perspective, are there differences in audit logs and KMS support between hosted and dedicated/private?
[03:14] Samantha: hosted supports audit logs and KMS integration, but Dedicated gives you customer-dedicated tenants and optional VPC peering or private link — and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control over keys and network. for SOC2/ISO requirements, many enterprises choose Dedicated or Private.
[03:33] Priya: we need to ensure no model weights leave our environment. Private on-prem would be ideal but we prefer a managed dedicated pool if it meets encryption-at-rest and key control needs. is that possible?
[03:44] Samantha: yes — Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed keys and VPC-only endpoints to meet those constraints. there are limits on available regions for Private/on-prem but Dedicated is widely available.
[03:57] Evan: about throughput guarantees — what's in the SLA and how do you measure it?
[04:04] Diego: SLA is per capacity unit: guaranteed baseline throughput per GPU type, with burst policies. measurement is via token-per-second metrics and p95 latency windows. if we miss a contractual throughput target repeatedly, credits or remediation plans kick in. we'll share the Dedicated SLA doc.
[04:22] Marcus: can you walk through an example workload test you would run for us? like model X with 1k context, 50 tokens gen, 200 qps?
[04:31] Diego: yes. typical bench: 1) baseline cold start latency (no cache), 2) warm cache p95 with sticky routing, 3) pooled batching p95/throughput, 4) stress test with noisy tenant simulation. for your setup we'd use your prompt set, simulate 200 qps with 20% bursts to 400 qps and measure p50/p95/p99 and tail noise.
[04:56] Priya: noisy tenant simulation — can you emulate realistic co-tenancy?
[05:01] Diego: we replay mixed workloads on the same pool to emulate contention. on hosted we add background noisy traffic to see eviction and queuing. on Dedicated we add synthetic tenants to stress the scheduler to confirm isolation boundaries.
[05:15] Samantha: real quick — about batching: what's the difference between continuous batching in hosted runtime and user-level batching in Dedicated?
[05:23] Aisha: hosted runtime uses adaptive continuous batching to maximize throughput while meeting latency SLOs; it automatically coalesces small requests. Dedicated lets you tune batching parameters (max batch size, latency target) and you can also carve GPU pools for different batch profiles. that gives more predictable throughput when you control batch windows.
[05:42] Evan: does adjusting batch size change model quality? sometimes we see hallucinations increase with longer gen due to micro-timing?
[05:50] Diego: batch size shouldn't change model semantics, but changing decode settings (temp, sampling) or sequence truncation can. however, aggressive batching can increase latency for single-request flows if not tuned. the real effect is on throughput/cost and on tail latencies, not on output distribution.
[06:08] Marcus: can you quantify cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we need rough numbers to justify the move.
[06:15] Samantha: cost varies by commitment. hosted is pay-as-you-go with higher per-token cost but zero infra ops. Dedicated has lower unit cost at committed levels but requires monthly/annual reservation; there's also ops add-on for managed patches. we'll share a TCO spreadsheet.
[06:30] Priya: what about KV cache sizing — how do we estimate how much KV to reserve?
[06:36] Aisha: KV cache sizing is driven by unique prefix cardinality and average KV size per request. rule of thumb: if you have high prefix reuse (like re-ranking the same candidates) you need less KV per QPS. we can run a profiler on your prompt set to estimate hits/misses and recommend memory per worker.
[06:55] Priya: profiler — is that something you run in a PoC?
[07:00] Diego: yes, as part of a pilot we run a profiler and a micro-bench. it outputs expected cache hit rate, optimal batch size, and expected p95 under dedicated vs hosted. we'll request the sample prompt set and a small traffic trace.
[07:12] Marcus: curious about quantization again — do you support mixed-precision kernels or INT8 on-prem?
[07:19] Aisha: runtime supports fp16, bf16, and int8 paths depending on hardware. INT8 kernels are available for some models and OSS forks; on Dedicated we can enable specific kernel stacks. on on-prem we can also inject custom kernels if customer requires. quality/regression testing is recommended after quant.
[07:36] Tara: for our audit, we need deterministic logging of requests, model version used, and KVC hit/miss per request. do you capture those at invocation-level?
[07:46] Diego: yes we emit traces with model version, route, worker id (or alias), KV hit/miss, batch size, and latency buckets. in Hosted we redact tenant-sensitive fields; in Dedicated/Private we can provide full logs into your S3/Kinesis endpoint depending on setup.
[08:02] Priya: great. are there limitations to sticky routing when you failover or during autoscale events?
[08:09] Diego: failover introduces cold cache misses; we have a warm-up strategy and proactive rehydration but you'll see transient p95 bumps. autoscale can cause rebalancing which again may evict cache. Dedicated gives you headroom to scale horizontally with less eviction if you set reserve capacity and warm pools.
[08:27] Marcus: for SLA testing, can we get a dedicated test window on your infra to run our burst tests?
[08:33] Samantha: yes, we can schedule a bench window on a dedicated pool or run it in hosted test environment with noise injection. recommended path: start with hosted simulation (faster), then move to Dedicated pilot to validate production numbers.
[08:47] Evan: any special networking considerations for VPC peering? e.g., latency added by private link?
[08:53] Diego: private link adds minimal hops — typically <3ms added egress depending on region. for strict low-latency needs, on-prem is ideal. Dedicated with VPC peering usually meets sub-10ms intra-region network SLOs. we'll share network topology docs.
[09:07] Priya: can you explain the billing model for burst capacity in Dedicated? we need to understand overage.
[09:14] Samantha: Dedicated includes baseline reserved capacity. you can configure burst policies with on-demand billing for peak—those are billed at a premium. there are also queue/backpressure policies to prevent noisy tenants from consuming bursts.
[09:30] Marcus: on the runtime side, can you control kernel selection or is that automatic? we have some custom kernels for our models.
[09:37] Aisha: kernel selection is automatic but you can pin kernel profiles in Dedicated or Private. if you have custom kernels we can discuss a validation process for on-prem or dedicated pools.
[09:48] Tara: for compliance, how long are logs retained and do you support customer-managed retention?
[09:55] Diego: retention policies are configurable. Hosted default is 90 days with redaction options. Dedicated/Private you can set retention or export logs to your archive. we also support audit export to your SIEM.
[10:05] Samantha: ok quick recap — Diego will run a bench on an 8x A100 equiv dedicated test, Aisha will profile KV hit rates once we get the prompt set, I'll send pricing and SLA, and customer will provide the sample prompts and target metrics.
[10:18] Priya: timeline — can we get preliminary numbers next week? we have execs wanting a cost/latency bounding for approval.
[10:24] Samantha: yes we'll aim for initial bench results by 2026-09-16 and pricing same week.
[10:28] Marcus: small nit — when you run the bench, please include breakdown of token compute vs memory wait times, and per-request KV hit percentage.
[10:36] Diego: will do, we'll provide flamegraph-like breakdowns and trace logs.
[10:40] Evan: what's the expected delta in ops effort if we go Dedicated vs Hosted? our platform team bandwidth is limited.
[10:46] Samantha: Dedicated requires coordination: capacity reservations, some network setup (VPC/VPN), and optional agent install for private environments. we offer managed ops add-on to handle patching and upgrades. hosted is lowest ops overhead.
[10:58] Marcus: about cold start — how long does it take to spin up warm workers from zero on Dedicated?
[11:04] Aisha: cold start depends on model size and image layering. baseline cold can be 20-60s for large models if the pool is empty. with warm pools and pre-warmed instances it's sub-second for routing but that costs reserved memory.
[11:18] Priya: are there best practices to reduce cold starts without huge cost?
[11:22] Diego: keep a small warm worker pool for your critical routes, use proactive cache prewarm scripts during deployments, and use gradual rollout to avoid worst-case cold storms.
[11:33] Tara: for on-prem, do you support HSM-based key storage?
[11:37] Samantha: yes, Private supports HSM/KMS integration and customer-managed key lifecycle.
[11:41] Evan: any gotchas about model version pinning and rollback?
[11:45] Aisha: you can pin version per route and we support canary rollouts. if you rollback you'll need to consider cache invalidation; we have tooling to bulk invalidate KV entries tied to model versions.
[11:58] Priya: ok this is super helpful. last question: for our re-ranker, if we get to 500 qps sustained, is Dedicated the only viable option?
[12:06] Diego: not necessarily — hosted can handle 500 qps if you pay for sufficient provision and accept some transient tail risk. Dedicated makes it more predictable and often cheaper at that sustained level. if you want strict p95 SLOs and isolation, Dedicated is recommended.
[12:24] Samantha: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and bench times. any final questions?
[12:29] Priya: none here, thanks.
[12:31] Marcus: thanks all.

End of transcript.
